subject.title: Preserve structured ACP backend error kinds instead of mapping all errors to `end_turn`

question: Should non-refusal Gateway chat failures in the ACP bridge reject `session/prompt` with structured `RequestError`, or keep resolving `PromptResponse` while exposing structured failure data through another approved surface?
rationale: The requested behavior is real, but the ACP SDK stop-reason contract lacks the requested backend failure kinds and switching prompt settlement to JSON-RPC rejection is a client-visible compatibility choice.

options.title: Approve RequestError settlement after fixes
options.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures after avoiding SDK code conflicts, keeping reconnect behavior intentional, and requiring real ACP proof.

options.title: Preserve resolved prompt responses
options.body: Keep resolved `PromptResponse` as the default and expose structured backend error data only through an explicitly approved metadata or diagnostic surface.

options.title: Pause for a replacement
options.body: Leave this issue open for a maintainer-led or refreshed implementation if the current branch cannot settle the compatibility contract and proof gap.

recommendation.title: Approve RequestError settlement after fixes
recommendation.body: Use rejected `session/prompt` responses for backend failures after avoiding SDK code conflicts, keeping reconnect behavior intentional, and requiring real ACP proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner signal is tied to the current ACP error-kind classification and tests, which makes it the best available routing point for the contract decision.
